messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

I don’t have dates or times to offer yet, and I’m not sure what changes I could make. I’d prefer the trailer not stay on my pad, but I rent and need my landlord’s approval before changing the arrangement; I haven’t asked him. Any pickup or return would need clear notice and access kept open. It would help if you and C worked out the schedule directly and let me know what you’re proposing, rather than leaving me to choose between you.

I need the trailer for my own home project within the next few weeks, and I won’t wait until A is finished. I can’t give full dates, times, duration, or changeable dates yet; those aren’t set. Pickup and return need clear notice and open access to B’s pad. I don’t know about any landlord approval requirement. A handoff at work could help if we agree on timing.

I want to use it for weekend trips in the next few weeks, but I don’t have specific dates or pickup and return times yet. I can discuss moving dates, but there’s no firm deadline beyond settling this within a few weeks; trip length and handoff details aren’t set. We need to coordinate access, notice, and parking with B since it’s on B’s pad. I don’t know of any issue with the pad. A handoff at work could help with keys, but not with getting the trailer from B’s place.
Two days’ notice and a named contact work. I can’t agree to keeping the trailer on my pad as an ongoing arrangement; I’d need my landlord’s approval for any change.

I can’t give full dates or times yet; I haven’t set them. My trips are weekends in the next few weeks, and I don’t know their length or which dates I could change. I need pickup and return arranged with clear notice and access. I now know B needs landlord approval for pad changes, so that needs checking; I won’t assume the trailer can be moved or parked elsewhere. A handoff at work could help with keys if we agree on timing, but the trailer still needs to be picked up and returned at B’s pad.

Accept, with one change: schedule my short home-project period independently, not after A’s trips. Exact dates and times aren’t set; my proposal is the first available short period in the next few weeks, with the next available non-overlapping period as backup.

Accept. I can’t give exact dates or times yet. My proposed period is the first mutually workable weekend in the next few weeks; backup is another mutually workable weekend. Trip length and pickup/return times are still to be agreed. Your questions don’t change my earlier reply; a work handoff could help with keys, but not trailer pickup.
Any change to what’s kept on my pad, including continued trailer parking, needs my landlord’s approval. I haven’t asked him, so I can’t confirm what I can allow yet.
Accept the structure. I can’t name a proposed weekend or backup yet; dates and times aren’t set. The later questions don’t change my earlier reply.
I accept the process. I haven’t asked my landlord yet, so I can’t confirm what I can allow. I’ll ask and let you know.

Accept, conditionally. My period’s length and backup are not set, and dates and times aren’t set. I still need the first available short period independently, subject to B confirming what parking and access are allowed.
Accept the revised plan with C’s change. I can wait for B’s confirmation. My dates, times, trip length, and backup are still not set.
